brief: UBS's weekly flow note argues hedge fund (HF) equity positioning is more constructive than the week's headline index moves suggest. Early-week HF selling was led by Hyperscalers, but Tech flows improved through the week led by Semis, and Friday's sell-off saw HFs buy the dip, including in Hyperscalers. Desks also saw Software and AI Industrials/Power buying, the latter mostly short-covering rather than outright. Derivs Tech upside demand was led by Memory (DRAM, EWY), concentrated on Wednesday, after SK Hynix's results beat but before Samsung's missed. Broad index flows flipped from downside hedging early in the week ($35m premium on November downside) to SPX/QQQ upside structures later. Long-only (LO) flows turned defensive, selling crowded names into defensives. Asia was mixed: Japan Tech bought after weeks of HF degrossing, Korea was mixed, Taiwan sold, and China's HSTECH kept selling while CSI buyers stayed sidelined pending stabilization. Brazil's equities dip-bought then went two-way; FX unwound BRL shorts before fresh USDBRL downside. EURUSD and USDCNH downside demand persist; USDKRW downside profit-taking is starting as the KRW rally strengthens. Gold saw sovereign buying at 4k but the desk thinks gold is funding the AI sell-off, while Metals ETFs (GDXJ) saw strong buying. Rates show persistent USD receiver demand.
